I suppose that means that Clemens goes out - but what then happens to the International Section? Will Robin do it? And also, what about the capitalist side? Is Rath staying on, or what? I'm sorry to have to ask so many questions, but I'm very puzzled about the new Department. I just can't see how a staff of Robin, Margaret, Parsons and Packman can produce the Bulletin, Circular, do enquiries, and run the office. Do please enlighten me.

The opera and theatre season has just opened with a tremendous flourish. Have you ever seen Verdi's "Aida"? It's an opera which I had seen twice before in London, and thought it rather poor. But when I saw it at the Bolshoi Theatre the other night, I thought it one of the best shows I had ever seen or heard. God, they do know how to stage things here.

Was the Theatre of the Revolution in existence when you were here? Trilby and I went there to see Ernst Toller's "Massen Menschen" - and though we didn't understand a single word, neither of us had ever seen anything like it in all our lives. I wish I could describe it to you, but it would sound quite mad. I'll have a shot. The actors play on several planes. There is one fixed set which never changes throughout the play, except for minor details. The scenery is made of rough wood, and looks rather like a man's carpenter's shop. On one side there is an escalator leading from one plank to another, and on the other side there is a spiral staircase, looking rather like a windmill, on the top of which people danced wildly. Then a sloping plank led up to the centre of the stage, so that all the groups verged to this central spot. The whole effect was simply marvellous.
